monitors.confirmDelete: Delete this monitor and its history?

monitors.pausedNotice: Paused: no checks run and no alerts are sent. Resume to start checking again.
monitors.sloHint: Sets this monitor's monthly error budget: the downtime you can afford before missing the target.
monitors.dependsOnHint: While that monitor is down, this one's failures are recorded but nobody is alerted. If it recovers and this one is still down, you are alerted then.
monitors.groupAlerts: Send one message when several monitors in this group fail together
monitors.groupAlertsHint: Applies to the whole group. Alerts wait up to 15 seconds to collect the failures.
monitors.noChecksYet: No checks yet. The first results arrive within one interval, or use Test now.
monitors.secretsRetarget: This monitor has saved credentials (a password, token or secret header). They were entered for the old target and won't be sent to the new one.
monitors.secretsDrop: Remove the saved credentials and save
monitors.secretsRetargetRequired: The target changed: confirm removing the saved credentials, or keep the old target.
monitors.confirmRegions: Open an incident when it fails from
monitors.confirmRegionsHint: A failure in one region is rechecked from the others first. Fewer regions alert sooner; more regions mean fewer false alarms.
monitors.alertRegionalHint: When it fails from fewer regions than that and the others are healthy, open a low-severity incident instead of only showing the monitor as degraded.
monitors.reducedConfirmation: Our checks from {regions} aren't reliable right now because of a problem on our side, so they don't count. This monitor is still checked from its other regions, with fewer of them to confirm an outage. You don't need to do anything.
monitors.notWatched: This monitor is only checked from {regions}, and our checks from there aren't working right now because of a problem on our side. It isn't being watched until that is fixed. We have been alerted and are on it.

integrations.slackInstalled: Slack is connected. Pick a channel to finish.
integrations.slackNoInstall: Install the Watchpost app in your Slack workspace first.

integrations.telegramWaiting: Waiting for you to press Start in Telegram…

slack.summary: Install the Watchpost app and pick a channel. Follow-ups reply in the alert's thread.
slack.steps:
Click Add to Slack and approve the app for your Slack workspace.
Pick the channel alerts should go to.
For a private channel, invite the Watchpost app to it first.

slack-webhook.summary: Post to one Slack channel through an incoming webhook, without installing our app.
slack-webhook.steps:
At api.slack.com/apps, create an app (From scratch) and turn on Incoming Webhooks.
Click Add New Webhook to Workspace and pick the channel.
Copy the webhook URL and paste it below.

teams.summary: Adaptive Cards in a Teams channel through a Workflows webhook.
teams.steps:
In Teams, open the channel's ⋯ menu and choose Workflows.
Pick “Send webhook alerts to a channel” and finish the wizard.
Copy the URL it shows and paste it below.

discord.summary: Colored embeds in a Discord channel. The first message updates as the incident changes.
discord.steps:
In Discord, open Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks.
Click New Webhook and pick the channel.
Copy the webhook URL and paste it below.

telegram.summary: Our bot posts to a chat or group. Follow-ups reply to the first message.
telegram.steps:
Give it a name and save.
Open the link we show in Telegram and press Start.
For a group, add the bot to the group and open the link there.

google-chat.summary: Cards in a Google Chat space. An incident's updates stay in one thread.
google-chat.steps:
In the space, open its menu → Apps & integrations → Webhooks.
Add a webhook named Watchpost.
Copy its URL and paste it below.

mattermost.summary: Alerts in a Mattermost channel through an incoming webhook.
mattermost.steps:
In Mattermost, open Integrations → Incoming Webhooks → Add Incoming Webhook.
Pick the channel and save.
Copy the webhook URL and paste it below. The server must be reachable from the internet over HTTPS.

rocketchat.summary: Alerts in a Rocket.Chat channel through an incoming webhook.
rocketchat.steps:
In Rocket.Chat, open Administration → Workspace → Integrations → New → Incoming.
Enable it, pick the channel and the user to post as, and save.
Copy the Webhook URL and paste it below. The server must be reachable from the internet over HTTPS.

zulip.summary: A bot posts to a Zulip channel, with one topic per monitor.
zulip.steps:
In Zulip, open Settings → Personal → Bots and add a bot (the Incoming webhook type is enough).
Copy the bot's email and API key.
Subscribe the bot to the channel, then fill in the form.

matrix.summary: A bot account posts to a Matrix room. Follow-ups go in a thread.
matrix.steps:
Create a Matrix account for the bot, invite it to the room and accept the invite.
Copy the bot's access token (in Element: Settings → Help & About → Advanced).
Copy the room's internal ID (Room settings → Advanced). It starts with !.

pagerduty.summary: Page your on-call through PagerDuty. Acknowledging or resolving here does the same there.
pagerduty.steps:
In PagerDuty, open the service → Integrations → Add an integration → Events API V2.
Copy the Integration Key.
Paste it below and pick your account's region.

opsgenie.summary: Alerts in Opsgenie, acknowledged and closed in step with the incident.
opsgenie.steps:
In Opsgenie, open your team → Integrations → Add integration → API.
Turn the integration on and copy its API key.
Paste it below and pick your region.
opsgenie.note: Opsgenie shuts down on April 5, 2027. After you move to Jira Service Management, switch the region here; the alert format stays the same.

jira-service-management.summary: Alerts in Jira Service Management operations, where Opsgenie's alerting now lives.
jira-service-management.steps:
In Jira Service Management, open your team's Operations → Integrations → Add integration → API.
Turn the integration on and copy its API key.
Paste it below.

splunk-on-call.summary: Page through Splunk On-Call (VictorOps). Acknowledgements and recoveries follow the incident.
splunk-on-call.steps:
In Splunk On-Call, open Integrations → 3rd Party Integrations → REST – Generic and enable it.
Copy the endpoint URL.
Replace $routing_key at its end with a routing key from Settings → Routing Keys, and paste it below.

pushover.summary: Push notifications to phones through your own Pushover application.
pushover.steps:
On pushover.net, create an application and copy its API token.
Copy your user key, or a delivery group's key, from the dashboard.
Paste both below.

ntfy.summary: Push notifications through ntfy.sh or your own ntfy server.
ntfy.steps:
Pick a topic name that is hard to guess: anyone who knows it can read your alerts.
Subscribe to the topic in the ntfy app.
For a protected topic, or to use your own account's limits on ntfy.sh, add an access token.

pushbullet.summary: Pushes to all your devices, or to the subscribers of a Pushbullet channel.
pushbullet.steps:
On pushbullet.com, open Settings → Account → Create Access Token.
Paste the token below.
To push to a channel instead of your own devices, enter its tag.

gotify.summary: Messages to your self-hosted Gotify server.
gotify.steps:
In Gotify, open Apps → Create Application and copy its token. It is shown once.
Enter your server's address and the token below.
The server must be reachable from the internet over HTTPS.

email.summary: Alert emails with one-click acknowledge and resolve links.
email.steps:
Enter up to 10 addresses, separated by commas.
Each person gets their own email with their own action links.

webhook.summary: Signed JSON for every incident event, to any HTTP endpoint.
webhook.steps:
Enter the URL that should receive POST requests.
Add headers if your endpoint needs them, for example Authorization.
After saving, copy the signing secret to verify the Watchpost-Signature header.

zapier.summary: Start a Zap from every incident event with Webhooks by Zapier.
zapier.steps:
In Zapier, create a Zap with the trigger Webhooks by Zapier → Catch Hook.
Copy the webhook URL Zapier shows and paste it below.
Send a test from here, then map the fields in your Zap.

make.summary: Start a Make scenario from every incident event.
make.steps:
In Make, add a Webhooks → Custom webhook module to a scenario.
Copy its address and paste it below.
Send a test from here so Make learns the data structure.

n8n.summary: Trigger an n8n workflow from every incident event.
n8n.steps:
In n8n, add a Webhook node with the method POST.
Copy its production URL and paste it below.
If the node uses header authentication, add that header here.

sms.summary: Text messages to a phone. Reply 1 to acknowledge or 2 to resolve. Uses alert credits.
sms.steps:
Enter the number in international format, like +14155550123.
Check what a message to that country costs in credits, then send a code to the number.
Enter the code to verify the number, then save.

voice.summary: A phone call that reads the alert aloud. Press 1 to acknowledge. Uses alert credits.
voice.steps:
Enter the number in international format, like +14155550123.
Check what a call to that country costs in credits, then send a code to the number by SMS.
Enter the code to verify the number, then save. Calls are placed for new and ongoing incidents only.

inbound.title: Inbound alerts
inbound.hint: Let your other tools open and close incidents here: Prometheus Alertmanager, Grafana, Datadog, anything that can post JSON, or email. A repeat of an open alert adds nothing, and the tool's recovery closes the incident.
inbound.name: Name
inbound.shownOnce: Copy it now. It is shown only once; anyone who has it can open incidents in this workspace. "New URL" replaces it.

setup.generic: POST JSON with at least a title. Use status "trigger" or "resolve" and the same dedup_key on both.
setup.alertmanager: In alertmanager.yml add a receiver with webhook_configs: url set to this URL, and send_resolved: true.
setup.grafana: In Grafana add a contact point of type Webhook with this URL, and leave "Disable resolved message" off.
setup.datadog: In Datadog's Webhooks integration add a webhook with this URL and this payload, then mention it in a monitor's message:
setup.email: Point your inbound-mail provider's webhook at this URL. It should post JSON with from, subject and text; a subject starting with RECOVERY, RESOLVED or OK closes the incident.

inbound.payloadHint: Paste what the tool sends, as JSON. Nothing is opened: this only shows what would happen.

heartbeats.title: Heartbeats
heartbeats.intro: Cron jobs and workers ping a URL; we alert when a ping is late or reports a failure.
heartbeats.urlOnce: Copy it now: it's shown only once. You can create a new one at any time.
heartbeats.usage: Add to the end of your job: curl -fsS {url}

roleHints.admin: Everything except deleting the workspace: monitors, integrations, alert routing, members and billing.
roleHints.member: Manages monitors, maintenance and incidents. Can't change integrations, members or billing.
roleHints.responder: Sees everything and can acknowledge, resolve and comment on incidents. Can't change monitors.
roleHints.viewer: Read-only: sees monitors, incidents and maintenance, changes nothing.
roleHints.billing: Billing pages only: the plan, usage, credits and invoices. Sees no monitors or incidents.

oncall.lead: Who gets paged, and when. Each schedule rotates through its people; overrides cover a stretch by hand.
oncall.emptyHintAdmin: Create one to say who is on call each week. Until then, alerts go to every channel in your alert routes.
oncall.emptyHint: An admin can create one. Until then, alerts go to every channel in your alert routes.

oncall.overridesHint: Put someone on call for a stretch, whatever the rotation says: cover a doctor's appointment, swap a weekend.
oncall.overrideTimes: The override must end after it starts.

feed.title: Your on-call calendar
feed.hint: Subscribe from Google Calendar, Outlook or Apple Calendar to see your own shifts next to your meetings. The link is private: anyone who has it can see when you are on call.

mine.notNow: You are not on call right now.

oncall.importFromOpsgenie: Moving from Opsgenie? Import your schedules and escalation policies.

imports.title: Import from another tool
imports.lead: Preview first: you see what every monitor, schedule and escalation policy would become here, and what can't come over and why. Nothing is created until you say so.
imports.adminsOnly: Importing creates monitors and schedules in bulk, so it is for admins and owners.

how.uptimerobot: Give a read-only API key (UptimeRobot → Integrations & API → Read-only API key), or paste the JSON answer of the getMonitors API.
how.uptime_kuma: In Uptime Kuma open Settings → Backup, export, and paste the file's contents.
how.better_stack: Paste the JSON answer of Better Stack's monitors API (GET /api/v2/monitors). To bring heartbeats too, paste an object with "monitors" and "heartbeats", each holding that API's answer.
how.opsgenie: Paste an object with "schedules" and "escalations", each holding the data list from Opsgenie's API (GET /v2/schedules?expand=rotation and GET /v2/escalations). People are matched to members here by email, so invite them first.

statusPages.what: Public status pages on your own domain, with components, 90-day uptime bars, incident updates and subscribers.
statusPages.meanwhile: Until then, every monitor page shows 90-day uptime and response times you can share with your team.

reports.what: Monthly SLA reports as PDF and CSV, and uptime history you can send to clients.
reports.meanwhile: A weekly digest already arrives by email every Monday, and the overview shows alert accuracy, response times and error budgets.

marketing.hero: Know about real outages first. Confirmed, explained, actionable.
marketing.subhead: Watchpost checks your sites and APIs from around the world, confirms each failure before it pages anyone, and lets your team acknowledge from wherever they are.
marketing.featuresTitle: Alerts you can trust at 3 a.m.
marketing.featuresIntro: Every alert is checked from more than one place and arrives with what you need to act on it.

confirmed.title: Confirmed before it pages you
confirmed.body: A failure is rechecked from other regions first, so one flaky network path doesn't wake anyone up.

evidence.title: Evidence in every alert
evidence.body: Each alert says what failed, the likely cause and what to check first, with the timings from every region.

channels.title: Alerts where your team works
channels.body: Email, Slack, Teams, Discord, Telegram, webhooks and more, with rules per channel and acknowledge links that work from a phone.

changes.title: What changed before the outage
changes.body: Deploys from CI and GitHub, certificate and address changes and settings edits sit on the incident timeline.

tuning.title: Less noise over time
tuning.body: The tuning advisor finds flapping and false alarms and suggests fixes you can apply in one click.

heartbeats.title: Cron jobs and error budgets
heartbeats.body: Heartbeat monitors catch jobs that stop running, and monthly error budgets show which services are at risk.

faq.q1: Is the Free plan really free?
faq.a1: Yes. It has no time limit, needs no card and may be used for commercial projects.
faq.q2: What happens when the 14-day trial ends?
faq.a2: The workspace moves to the Free plan unless you choose a paid one. Nothing is deleted: monitors over the Free limits are paused and you pick which ones stay active.
faq.a3: No. Free includes 3 team members, Starter 5, and Pro and Business have unlimited members at the same price.
faq.q4: How do I pay, and what about tax?
faq.a4: Payments go through Paddle, which accepts cards and other common methods, adds tax where it applies and issues the invoices. You can download invoices from the billing page.
faq.q5: Can I change or cancel my plan?
faq.a5: At any time. An upgrade starts at once. A move to a smaller plan or a cancellation takes effect at the end of the period you already paid for. Your data is kept either way.
faq.a6: Credits pay for SMS and voice alerts. Paid plans include some every month and you can buy more. Credits used by an incident you mark as a false alarm are returned. SMS and voice alerts are coming soon.
faq.q7: What does "Coming soon" mean in the table?
faq.a7: The feature is planned but not available yet. It will be added to the plans shown at no extra cost.

opsgenie.metaTitle: An Opsgenie alternative with monitoring built in
opsgenie.title: Moving on from Opsgenie? Bring your schedules with you.
opsgenie.lead: Watchpost has on-call schedules, escalation policies and alerts by push, email, SMS and phone call, together with the uptime monitoring that finds the problem in the first place. Import your Opsgenie schedules and escalations, run both side by side, and switch when you trust it.
opsgenie.noCard: No card needed. Every workspace starts with a 14-day Pro trial.
opsgenie.dateSales: New Opsgenie sales ended on June 4, 2025.
opsgenie.dateSupport: Support for Opsgenie ends on April 5, 2027.
opsgenie.dateData: Data that has not been migrated by then is deleted.
opsgenie.datesNote: Reported by the sources below, checked on {date}. Confirm the dates for your own account with Atlassian.

schedules.title: On-call schedules
schedules.body: Layers, daily and weekly rotations, working-hours windows and overrides, with handoffs that keep their clock time across daylight-saving changes. A private calendar link shows your shifts next to your meetings.

escalation.title: Escalation policies
escalation.body: Page a person or whoever is on call, then the next step after the minutes you choose, for as many rounds as you want. An acknowledgement stops it.

reach.title: Reach people where they are
reach.body: Each person sets their own rules: a notification on their phone and an email at once, a text after two minutes, a call after five. Acknowledge from the notification, the text or the call.

chat.title: Slack and Telegram, both ways
chat.body: Alerts carry Acknowledge and Resolve buttons, and /watchpost answers who is on call or starts a maintenance window.

inbound.title: Alerts from your other tools
inbound.body: Prometheus Alertmanager, Grafana, Datadog, generic JSON and email open and close incidents here, without duplicates.

monitoring.title: Monitoring included
monitoring.body: HTTP, keyword, TCP, ping, DNS, SSL and domain expiry checks and heartbeats from several regions, with a failure confirmed before anyone is paged.

import.title: Import.
import.body: Export your schedules and escalations with two API calls and paste them in. You see what each one becomes before anything is created.

parallel.title: Run side by side.
parallel.body: Watchpost can open and close alerts in Opsgenie or Jira Service Management, so your team keeps being paged the old way while you compare.

switch.title: Switch.
switch.body: Choose the escalation policy your alerts page through, run an alert drill, and turn the old integration off.

honest.heartbeats: Opsgenie heartbeats, teams and routing rules are not imported; heartbeats and alert routes are set up here by hand.
honest.integrations: Opsgenie's long list of integrations is replaced by the inbound sources above plus webhooks. If a tool you need is missing, tell us.
honest.mobile: There is no native mobile app yet. Watchpost installs from the browser as an app with notifications; on iPhone it must be added to the Home Screen first.

opsgenie.pricingBody: Plans have one price per workspace, not per seat. On-call schedules and escalation policies are part of the Starter plan and up; Pro and Business have no limit on members, schedules or policies. SMS and calls use prepaid alert credits.
